To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the orientation of the asymmetric localization of PAR protein in C. elegans germline precells is determined by the extracellular cues.
PAR-2 localization in P2 and P1 germline precursers is asymmetric and determined by extracellular signaling via MES-1 and SRC-1.
the orientation of PAR-2 localization in the P3 cell is determined by contact of the endodermal precursor cell with the P3 cell, and this process requires the MES-1/Src-1 signaling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that determine the orientation of PAR protein localization in C. elegans germline precursers.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the establishment of the asymmetric cell division in C. elegans germline precursers.
the mechanisms by which the orientation of the axis of asymmetric cell divisions is established during development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the asymmetric PAR protein localization in the C. elgans embryo is controlled by a complex combination of both extracellular and intracellular signals.
the axis of asymmetric PAR protein localization is determined by extracellular signals in the P2-P3 germline precursor cells.
extracellular signals control PAR protein localization during the asymmetric cell division in P2 and P2 cells in C. elegans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the orientation of asymmetric cell division in C. elegans germline precusors is controlled by contact with endoermal precursor cells.
PAR-2 localization in the P0 and germline precusor cells (P1-P3) is asymmetric, but the orientation is controlled by extrinsic cues.
the orientation of the PAR protein localization is controlled by extracellualr signaling in the P2/P3 cell divisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the asymmetric localization of PAR-1 and PAR-2 proteins in the C. Elegans embryo is determined by extracellular signals.
the axis of asymmetric cell divisions is determined by extracellular signals in the P2/P3 cell lineage in C. elegans.
the orientation of PAR protein localization is controlled by extrinsic cues.
